$absentKeyRationaleComment: Machine-read by tests/link/test_object_format_family_symmetry.cpp: every root key a SIBLING of this format declares and this file does not must appear below with a non-empty reason, and every entry below must correspond to a real absence. Both directions fail loud, so this table can neither be skipped nor rot after a gap is closed. CREATED 2026-08-19 (cycle P12) the moment the arm64 dylib sibling opted into tlsAccess -- before that this file had no absent sibling key and therefore no table.

$absentKeyRationale.tlsAccess: DELIBERATE: the arm64 dylib sibling's TLS opt-in (D-LK3-DYLIB-TLS-MODEL, closed 2026-08-19) rides the SHARED macho-tlv walker machinery, but x86_64 Darwin TLS depends on the x86_64 EXEC's own TLS opt-in (macho64-x86_64-darwin-exec deliberately declares no tlsAccess -- its $absentKeyRationale, pinned by Linker.TdataItemOnNonOptedInFormatsRejectsAtAcceptsGate, and MEASURED zero _Thread_local consumers in the staged upstream corpus; the sibling's Rosetta run leg landed 2026-08-19, so nothing here waits on runtime reachability). A _Thread_local TU on this format walls loud (K_FormatLacksThreadLocalSupport / the supportedDataSections gate), which is the correct outcome until an x86_64 Darwin TLS cycle lands.

$comment: Mach-O 64-bit DYNAMIC LIBRARY (MH_DYLIB, .dylib) for x86_64 macOS -- c171 conformance (the x86_64 sibling of macho64-arm64-darwin-dylib). CONFIG-ONLY for the writer: EVERY dylib divergence in `src/link/format/macho.cpp` is FILETYPE-keyed (`isDylib = filetype==Dylib`), never cputype-keyed -- MH_DYLIB routes unconditionally to `encodeExecDynamic` (the x86_64 macOS dynamic writer is in fact the ORIGINAL one, D-LK6-5); the sole cputype dispatch in the dynamic path is `__stubs` (`machoStubSizeFor` x86_64=6-byte FF 25 disp32, already supported); the export trie, ad-hoc code signing (execSegFlags is a caller-supplied per-flavor arg -- dylib=0, arch-neutral), and segment layout (`kPageSize = im.segmentPageSize`) are all arch-neutral. So this needs NO writer code, only this schema. Differs from macho64-arm64-darwin-dylib in ONLY the arch-specific fields: cputype (16777223 x86_64 vs 16777228 arm64), cpusubtype (3 vs 0), segmentPageSize (4096 x86_64 4 KiB pages vs 16384 Apple-Silicon 16 KiB), text virtualAddress (= segmentPageSize), longDoubleFormat (x87-80, x86_64's 80-bit extended -- arm64 uses IEEE-128 and omits it), and the reloc rows (X86_64_RELOC_* vs ARM64_RELOC_*). **RUNTIME IS macOS-x86_64/Rosetta-GATED**: there is NO macOS-x86_64 CI leg (macos-latest is Apple Silicon), so this ships with STRUCTURAL byte-pins ONLY (the writer emits it correctly -- proven at the byte level), and its exit-code RUN witness rides a future macOS-x86_64/Rosetta leg (the D-LK1-MACHO-X8664-DARWIN-DATA-SECTION untested-form discipline; follow-up D-LK-MACHO-X8664-DYLIB-RUNTIME). Code signing is KEPT (ad-hoc SHA-256) though x86_64 macOS does not REQUIRE it (unlike Apple Silicon) -- a signed dylib loads everywhere and mirrors modern ld64, which ad-hoc-signs all output.
$stackReserveUnsupportedReasonComment: D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH: a shared library carries an image header but NO field for a stack size (there is no LC_MAIN in a MH_DYLIB / no stack-size field in an ELF ET_DYN), and a loaded library never owns a thread's stack anyway, so a `stackReserve` / `--stack-reserve` request is REFUSED with an actionable remedy rather than silently dropped.
$dataModelComment: LP64 (64-bit Darwin: int 32, long 64, ptr 64) -- same as the x86_64 exec/object siblings.
$headerNameMatchingComment: D-PP-HEADER-CASE-INSENSITIVE-PE: macOS ships on APFS/HFS+ volumes that are CASE-INSENSITIVE by default (the installer default since 10.13; a case-sensitive volume is opt-in), and Apple's own SDK headers rely on it -- `<TargetConditionals.h>` / `<CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>` are routinely spelled with divergent case. REQUIRED closed-enum field. DSS ASCII-folds the comparison ITSELF per path component rather than delegating to fs::exists, so a Darwin cross-build from a case-sensitive Linux host resolves exactly as it does natively.
$cSymbolDecorationComment: D-FFI-CMANGLING-RULE-NOT-CONFIG-DRIVEN: Apple's C ABI prefixes EVERY C symbol with exactly ONE leading underscore, on both 32- and 64-bit Mach-O -- the rule has no bitness axis and no per-arch axis (the arm64 and x86_64 slices of the universal libSystem decorate identically), which is why it is declared per FORMAT and not per target. EVIDENCE, EACH LABELLED. MEASURED-BY-EXECUTION (recorded TF-C113, the macOS cross-build arc): a Windows host cross-emitted a mach-o arm64 binary whose only process-exit path is the `_exit` import, and it RAN on the operator's Apple Silicon Mac and exited correctly -- an undecorated `exit` would have been an unresolved dyld bind, not a cosmetic difference. MEASURED (recorded TF-C121): libSystem's x86_64 slice exports BOTH `_fstat` and `_fstat$INODE64`, i.e. the C identifier `fstat` reaches the linker as `_fstat`. NOT RE-MEASURED THIS CYCLE, stated rather than buried: the Mac is a personal machine and was not declared reachable, so nothing here rests on a probe taken today. This key is the single owner of a fact that previously had TWO: the closed C++ table `kCManglingRules` (src/ffi/mangling/c_mangle.cpp, keyed on ObjectFormatKind) and, redundantly, a literal encoding in the descriptors themselves -- the macho64-*-exec files spell `processExit.importMangledName` as `_exit` while their elf/pe siblings spell it `exit`. Two owners in two languages, with nothing forcing them to agree. RED-ON-DISABLE, stated precisely for the tier that exists today (MEASURED 2026-08-06 by actually removing the key from a shipped file and running the suite): DELETE this key and the format is REFUSED AT LOAD -- TWO errors at /cSymbolDecoration, one C_MissingField from the loader and one from ObjectFormatData::validate(), which loadFromText runs before returning -- so every test and example that loads this format goes red, naming the file. CHANGING the value is now an equally REAL lever, and this sentence was corrected the moment it became true: before step C4 the engine still read a C++ table and the value here changed no emitted binary. C4 landed (same cycle, TF-C122), and the effect is MEASURED 2026-08-06 -- flipping macho64-arm64-darwin-exec from `leading-underscore` to `none` and RECOMPILING NOTHING made the engine emit `printf` where it had emitted `_printf`, reddening tests/ffi/test_c_mangle.cpp's SchemeIsReadFromTheShippedSchemaNotACppTable. That is the whole point of the anchor: the answer lives in this file, so editing this file changes what the compiler emits. Two further pins guard the value: tests/link/test_c_symbol_decoration.cpp asserts the per-kind answer across all 24 shipped files and cross-checks it against this family's own processExit.importMangledName.
$cCallingConventionComment: D-FFI-ABI-CATALOG-SELECTS-CALLING-CONVENTION-BY-FORMAT-IDENTITY: the platform C ABI for code compiled into this format, NAMING a row in the paired target's callingConventions[] array. This selection used to be re-derived in C++ by `kAbiCatalog`, a closed table keyed on (target name, ObjectFormatKind) — while this very string was already written here. Two owners of one fact; the table is deleted and this is the single owner. System V AMD64 (`rdi,rsi,rdx,rcx,r8,r9`).
$outputExtensionComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: the extension the driver appends to an artifact this format produces. This used to be derived in C++ by `program/target_spec.cpp::outputExtensionFor`, a five-arm `switch (fmt.kind())` with a NESTED per-flavor switch inside each arm -- seven identity mentions computing a NAMING fact, which is not an engine behaviour at all. The nest existed because one ObjectFormatKind spans several artifact flavors; a DOCUMENT is exactly one flavor, so the whole derivation collapses to this one string. REQUIRED on every format. An EMPTY value is a DECLARED answer and not an omission -- a Unix executable carries no extension -- which is why the in-memory field is an `optional` and the loader's required check asks `contains`, never `empty`.
$archiveFlavorComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: WHICH `ar` variant this format's ECOSYSTEM uses. Declared on every native format, not only the `container: archive` ones, because that is what the deleted C++ derivation answered: `(format.kind() == ObjectFormatKind::Pe) ? Coff : SysV` was handed WHATEVER format the caller had, and `linkAndWriteStaticArchive` is reachable with the RELOCATABLE format of an ecosystem as well as its archive one (MEASURED -- restricting the key to archives reddened link/test_ar_writer and program/test_static_link). NOT cosmetic: the coff flavor carries the little-endian second linker member link.exe requires to resolve members at all. A closed VERB rather than an open name, because an archive layout is an ENGINE capability -- only variants `writeArArchive` realizes can be honored.
$targetArchComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: the .target.json NAME this format is for. `crossValidateTargetFormat` compares it against TargetSchema::name() -- two DECLARED NAMES -- where it used to run a six-arm `switch (format.kind())` reading a DIFFERENT field per identity (elf.machine / pe.machine / macho.cputype) and compare each against a hardcoded C++ table, kTargetArchMachineCodes, keyed on (target name x format kind). THAT TABLE IS DELETED, and the argument is ONE OWNER rather than tidiness: `arm64 is EM_AARCH64 = 183` had two owners -- this document's own machine field and that C++ row -- with nothing forcing them to agree, which is the identical shape as kCManglingRules and kAbiCatalog. The number now lives only in the document that emits it, and the pairing question is answered by a name this document states outright. Adding a new arch is now JSON-ONLY.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C97 (D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): the C-visible face of this file's `dataModel` above, DERIVED FROM THAT VALUE AND NEVER FROM THIS FILE'S NAME -- the loader synthesizes no macro name and the engine performs no format-identity branch; it merges whatever rows are declared here with the language's `preprocess.predefinedMacros` and the target's `predefinedMacros`, applying `availableObjectFormats` exactly once. DECLARED ON THE FORMAT because the data model is per-(OS x format), not per-CPU: the same x86_64 target is LP64 here and LLP64 under pe64-x86_64-windows-*, so a target-side row would be wrong on one of its own formats -- which is exactly what both .target.json files say when they record `__LP64__`/`_LP64` as DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED and defer to the format. BOTH spellings, each value 1: MEASURED 2026-07-30 with `/usr/bin/clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>` (Apple clang 21.0.0), __LP64__ and _LP64 are BOTH defined as 1 on arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-linux-gnu and x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, and NEITHER is defined on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. COLLISION POLICY: a name declared by this file AND the language or target config is FATAL (C_ConflictingPredefinedMacro) -- no side silently wins. WHAT IT UNBLOCKS, MEASURED: the macOS SDK gates 234 occurrences across 91 headers on __LP64__, so without these rows DSS compiled the SDK's ILP32 arms while its own widths were LP64 (sizeof(long)==8), and $SDK/usr/include/mach/port.h:113-114 then asserted the user32 struct size 12 instead of user64's 16 -- sqlite mem1.c's three error[S0029]. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this key and examples/c/predefined_lp64_macho stops exiting 42.
$longDoubleFormatComment: x86_64 macOS `long double` is the 80-bit x87 extended type (16-byte aligned) -- the same value the macho64-x86_64-darwin-exec sibling declares. ⚠ CORRECTED 2026-08-06: this comment used to end '(arm64 macOS uses IEEE-754 binary128 and its dylib omits this field.)', which was wrong TWICE and is worth recording rather than quietly deleting. Apple arm64 `long double` is `f64` (long double IS double), NOT binary128 -- binary128 is LINUX arm64, a different platform on the same CPU; and the arm64 dylib's omission was a GAP, not a design: it was the only arm64 Darwin format missing the axis, so `long double` compiled on the arm64 `.o` and `.exec` and was REJECTED on the `.dylib` (S0056) from the same source. The sibling now declares `f64` and the sentence that rationalised its absence is gone.
$bitFieldStrategyComment: D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-ABI-EXACT: Darwin x86_64 uses the generic LSB-first bit-field allocation -- same gnu_packed as the x86_64 macho siblings. ~~ CORRECTED P45 (D-CSUBSET-ZERO-WIDTH-BITFIELD-ALIGNMENT): the sentence above claiming Apple's arm64 divergences do NOT include bit-field allocation is MEASURED FALSE, and it is why the divergence went unmodelled. Apple DOES diverge on the alignment an UNNAMED bit-field contributes -- `struct { char c; unsigned :0; char d; }` is 5/1 on Apple arm64 and Apple x86_64 but 8/4 on generic AAPCS64 ELF (MEASURED: Apple clang 21.0.0 on the physical macOS host; gcc 13.3.0 + clang 18.1.3 per target). The PACKING claim the sentence was really making stands -- gnu_packed is still the right strategy here -- but the ALIGNMENT half is now carried by the separate `unnamedBitFieldAlignment` key below, which this document declares as `ignored`. A $comment asserting a settled answer gets probed LESS than a claim in code, which is the whole reason this correction is written in place rather than left to the next reader to re-derive.
$unnamedBitFieldAlignmentComment: D-CSUBSET-ZERO-WIDTH-BITFIELD-ALIGNMENT: an UNNAMED bit-field contributes NO alignment to the enclosing composite. MEASURED P45 -- `struct { char c; unsigned :0; char d; }` is 5/1 here, against 8/4 on the AAPCS64 ELF formats that share this very same `gnu_packed` strategy. ~ THIS IS AN APPLE DIVERGENCE FROM GENERIC AAPCS64, and this document's own `$bitFieldStrategyComment` asserted the opposite until P45. MEASURED on the physical macOS host with Apple clang 21.0.0 via `/usr/bin/clang -arch arm64`, rc=0. The zero-width field still BREAKS the packing cursor to its declared type's unit boundary (uncapped by `#pragma pack`); only the alignment contribution is dropped. ~ Declared on the FORMAT and not the target for exactly the reason `bitFieldStrategy` is: one CPU target serves several ABIs. There is NO target-side fallback for this key -- omitting it does not inherit, it leaves the axis undeclared and the layout engine fails loud the moment a zero-width bit-field needs it.
$externCallDispatchComment: The walker synthesizes a `__stubs` entry per extern FUNCTION (x86_64 = 6-byte FF 25 disp32 through the `__got` slot, lazy/eager per bindNow) and the call site is a plain direct `call rel32` to the stub -- pc-relative, slide-safe under the dyld base slide. D-FFI-EXTERN-CALL-DISPATCH.
$runtimeLibrariesComment: D-CSUBSET-PACKED-ATOMIC-MEMBER: this format's ROLE -> IMAGE table. It did not exist here before P53 because no spine block on this flavor named a role; `atomicsRuntime` below is the first, and the loader REFUSES a row no block names (inert config), so the two land together or not at all.
$atomicsRuntimeComment: D-CSUBSET-PACKED-ATOMIC-MEMBER: the GENERIC C11 atomics entry points an UNDER-ALIGNED `_Atomic` scalar access lowers to a CALL of, and the role naming the image that owns them. ★ THE NAMES ARE DECLARED HERE, ALREADY MANGLED FOR THIS FORMAT, for the reason `processExit.importMangledName` is: the C-level spelling is `__atomic_load`, but the SYMBOL a Mach-O image carries is `___atomic_load` — this format's own `cSymbolDecoration` leading underscore — and a lowerer re-deriving that rule would be the hardcoded-`msvcrt.dll` defect one tier over. ⚠⚠ THE GENERIC, RUNTIME-SIZED ENTRIES, NEVER THE SIZED `__atomic_load_4` FAMILY: ✔MEASURED 2026-09-02 on the native arm64 VPS, the sized entry SIGBUSes on the very access this block routes around (it is an IFUNC resolving to the inline realization), while the generic one dispatches through libatomic's lock table and returns the value — rc 42 against rc 135. A probe that calls the sized entry measures "no working reference exists", which is false. WHY THIS ROW POINTS AT THE IMAGE `cLibrary` ALREADY NAMES: ✔MEASURED — Apple clang links the packed case with `otool -L` showing `/usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib` ALONE and it runs rc 42; there is no `/usr/lib/libatomic*` on darwin, libSystem itself carries the entries. The role table PERMITS that sameness without ASSERTING it, which is the whole difference from a per-format CRT string, and `imageForRole` is nullopt-fail-loud so the row has to exist even though no new dylib reaches the link line. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this block and an under-aligned `_Atomic` access refuses at compile time under a `traps` target, naming this key.
$preemptibleDefinitionBindingsComment: D-MIR-DYLIB-SELF-CALL-BYPASSES-WEAK-COALESCING: WHICH of THIS ARTIFACT'S OWN externally-visible definitions its LOADER may replace with another image's definition of the same name -- so a call made INSIDE the artifact is routed through the loader (the format's ordinary `externCallDispatch` reference: an ELF PLT stub over a GOT slot, a Mach-O __got entry) instead of branching to the local body. Skipping that routing is a MEANING divergence, not a slow path: one process ends up holding two answers for one identifier, silently. MEASURED both rails. ELF: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 both emit `call <w@plt>` for a `.so`'s call to its own WEAK definition AND `call <st@plt>` for its own STRONG global one, and a DSS-built `.so` consumed by an executable that defines rival bodies returned its OWN answers (rc 4) where the gcc-built control returned the executable's (rc 6). Mach-O: dyld's two-level namespace coalesces only WEAK definitions (cycle P61 on Apple Silicon, same source: weak -> the consumer's answer rc 2, strong -> the dylib's own rc 1), so the Mach-O list is a STRICT SUBSET of the ELF one -- which is why this is DECLARED per format and not one hard-coded rule. VISIBILITY is NOT a member and never will be: a `static` or hidden-visibility definition is in no image's dynamic export set, so no loader can replace it under ANY format (MEASURED in the same object: both references leave those callees DIRECT while PLT-routing the default-visibility ones), and the engine checks it as a universal precondition. Absent on every EXEC/PIE flavour because the main executable is always its own winner; absent on every relocatable and static-library flavour because no loader is involved there; absent on pe64 because Windows has no symbol interposition.
$preemptibleDefinitionBindingsMachOComme: THE MACH-O REALIZATION, and it is what makes this declaration shippable rather than a loud refusal of a program Apple clang builds. The engine mints one loader-resolved reference per preemptible definition and routes the call through this format's externCallDispatch; the Mach-O walker encodes that reference into the LC_DYLD_INFO_ONLY WEAK BIND stream (weak_bind_off) -- a stream that carries NO dylib ordinal, which is precisely why dyld searches every loaded image for the coalescing winner instead of one named library. MEASURED 2026-09-06 on Apple Silicon (macOS 25.6.0, Apple clang 21.0.0 / ld-1267): ld64 emits `bind <weak-def-coalesce>/_w` on a __DATA_CONST __got slot for exactly this source, and the same source built -Wl,-no_fixup_chains puts it in weak_bind (bind_size 0, weak_bind_size 16, bytes 40 5f 77 00 51 71 00 90 00 ...) with the STRONG-global and `static` controls both staying DIRECT `bl` with an empty stream -- which is the measurement behind this list holding ONLY `weak` while the ELF documents hold [`global`, `weak`]. Before the walker could write those bytes this key was DELIBERATELY WITHHELD from the two darwin dylib documents, because declaring it would have turned a silent wrong answer into a loud refusal: both are defects, and the trade is not one a config edit gets to make quietly.
$weakDefinitionComment: D-CONFIG-WEAK-DEFINITION-DIALECT-NOT-DECLARED + D-LK-WEAK-DEFINITION-DIALECT-UNCONSULTED-BY-ELF-AND-MACHO-WRITERS: HOW this format spells a WEAK DEFINITION -- a symbol several translation units may define, of which the loader keeps one. Mach-O puts the weakness in a per-symbol FLAG BIT set ALONGSIDE an ordinary binding: N_WEAK_DEF (0x0080) in the nlist_64's n_desc, on a symbol that is otherwise N_SECT|N_EXT -- the same `symbol-flag` dialect this format's MH_OBJECT sibling declares, and read by the SAME `definedNDesc` in src/link/format/macho.cpp. THIS DECLARATION IS NEW IN THE CYCLE THAT CLOSED D-LK3-DYLIB-WEAK-EXPORT, AND ITS ABSENCE BEFORE THAT WAS ALSO AN ANSWER: the image walker used to REFUSE a weak definition outright, so a dialect declared here would have been a key nobody reads -- which drifts silently while reading as authoritative. The image arms now ENCODE one, so they owe the question, and `macho::encode` asks it ONCE above the filetype dispatch for every Mach-O arm (the shape `elf::encode` has had since it landed). AN IMAGE STATES MORE THAN THIS DIALECT -- the export trie terminal takes EXPORT_SYMBOL_FLAGS_WEAK_DEFINITION and the mach header takes MH_WEAK_DEFINES | MH_BINDS_TO_WEAK -- but both of those are CONTENT-DERIVED per module, exactly as MH_HAS_TLV_DESCRIPTORS is, and neither is or should become a config key: they are facts about THIS module, not about this format. THIS IS A DIALECT ROW, NOT A CAPABILITY FLAG: it says how this format spells something it CAN express, never that it cannot -- see D-LK-PE-ALTERNATENAME-DECLARE-AND-REFUSE for why an implementation gap recorded as a format incapability is a false fact in the place most likely to be trusted later. The loader additionally refuses this key at LOAD when the declared dialect is not one the resolved backend's walker writes (ObjectFormatBackend::weakDefinitionDialects), so a mis-declaration fails at its source rather than at the first weak definition.
$dataImportBindingComment: extern library DATA objects bind GOT-INDIRECT -- the walker reserves a `__got` slot per imported object; dyld's bind opcodes write the object's address into the slot and the GotIndirect lowering reads it. Copy relocations are not a Mach-O mechanism, and are no longer a DSS one either: the value was deleted from `DataImportBinding` (D-LK-ELF-COPY-RELOC-CLAIMS-ONE-NAME-OF-AN-ALIAS-SET).
$supportedDataSectionsComment: rodata (__TEXT,__const -- read-only), data (__DATA,__data), bss (__DATA,__bss zero-fill), relro (reloc-bearing const, __DATA,__const -- merged so its rebase slots land in writable pages). NO tdata/tbss: thread_local in a dylib needs the TLV descriptor model (D-LK3-DYLIB-TLS-MODEL); fails loud by this set's absence.
$artifactProfilesComment: This format SERVES the shared-library profile (plan 06 AP3). The cli profile is the exec sibling. ★ `module` JOINED THIS SET 2026-08-15 (plan 06 §5.1 B.12, as CORRECTED): a module IS a library, so it is served by every format that serves `lib` or `staticlib` and by nothing else. `artifactProfile` says what a project builds ITSELF as; `DependencyComposition` says how it is CONSUMED (`module` is SourceMerge — a consumer takes its SOURCES and ignores its artifact). Those are orthogonal, so a module builds standalone like any other library and the static-vs-dynamic choice is made by the `<target>:<format>` spec the author writes in `targets[]`, exactly as it already is for `lib` vs `staticlib` — no new rule and no engine change.

macho.$comment: mach_header_64 identity for an x86_64 MH_DYLIB. cputype = 16777223 (0x01000007 = CPU_TYPE_X86_64), cpusubtype = 3 (CPU_SUBTYPE_X86_64_ALL, same as the x86_64 exec). filetype = dylib (MH_DYLIB = 6). flags = 1048709 (MH_NOUNDEFS|MH_DYLDLINK|MH_TWOLEVEL|MH_NO_REEXPORTED_DYLIBS -- no MH_PIE on a library; same value as the arm64 dylib).

$codeSignatureIdentifierComment: D-LK-MACHO-CODESIGN-IDENTIFIER-IS-ONE-CONSTANT-FOR-EVERY-ARTIFACT: `image.codeSignature.identifier` is the CodeDirectory identOffset payload -- the artifact's CODE IDENTITY -- and until this cycle every darwin document declared a CONSTANT, so every artifact a format ever produced answered to one identity. MEASURED on the operator's Apple Silicon host (macOS 26.6.2, ld-1267), four arms driven by one instrument: two DSS dylibs sharing `com.dss.dylib`; the same two DSS dylibs with DISTINCT identifiers and nothing else changed; an ld64+`codesign -s -` pair with its default identifiers; and -- the decisive control -- an ld64+codesign pair FORCED to the same shared identifier. WHAT IS UNAFFECTED, and it is most of what one would guess: both dylibs dlopen, both link into one executable, both resolve to their own file under dladdr, `codesign --verify` returns 0 on each, and the same file mapped at two paths yields two images. The mechanism is that an ad-hoc signature's DESIGNATED REQUIREMENT is cdhash-keyed -- `codesign -d -r-` prints `designated => cdhash H"..."` on DSS and ld64 artifacts alike -- so the identifier never reaches dyld's load path. WHAT IS AFFECTED: identity-based requirement matching. A requirement `identifier "com.dss.dylib"` written for the first library ACCEPTS the second (rc 0 both), where the same requirement over distinct identifiers REFUSES (rc 3) and a cdhash requirement over those SAME two files REFUSES -- so the instrument discriminates and the identifier is what stops it. The forced-shared ld64 arm behaves identically, which is what says DSS's emitter is correct and the DECLARATION was the defect. Apple's own `codesign -s -` derives the identifier per artifact from the output's leaf name plus its LC_UUID (`alpha-55554944<uuid>`), so the reference never produces one identity for two artifacts by itself. RED-ON-DISABLE: revert this value to a constant and `MachoCodeSignatureIdentity.TwoArtifactsOfOneFormatGetDifferentIdentifiers` goes red -- it builds two artifacts from ONE format and compares the CodeDirectory identifier bytes it actually emitted. The walker RESOLVES this against the artifact named on the ImageRequest and REFUSES loud when it cannot; there is no fallback, because substituting something fixed is the defect itself.

image.$comment: Mach-O image fields for an x86_64 MH_DYLIB. pageZeroSize = 0 -- a dylib carries NO __PAGEZERO (validate() enforces): __TEXT.vmaddr = 0 and dyld slides the whole base-0 image. segmentPageSize = 4096 (0x1000) -- x86_64 macOS uses 4 KiB segment alignment (Apple Silicon's dylib uses 16384). NO dylinkerPath. installName = the LC_ID_DYLIB identity a client records, now a FUNCTION OF THE ARTIFACT rather than a constant -- see $installNameComment. loadDylibs = [libSystem] (the home of any libc import). bindNow = true. buildVersion macos 11.0. codeSignature = ad-hoc SHA-256: KEPT for symmetry with the arm64 dylib + modern ld64, though x86_64 macOS does not REQUIRE signing; the walker sets execSegFlags = 0 for the dylib flavor.
image.$installNameComment: D-LK-MACHO-DYLIB-INSTALL-NAME-IS-ONE-CONSTANT-FOR-EVERY-ARTIFACT: the LC_ID_DYLIB identity a CLIENT records at link time and dyld resolves at load, declared as a FUNCTION OF THE ARTIFACT BEING PRODUCED rather than as one string every dylib this format ever emits inherits. `${artifactFileName}` is substituted by the walker with the FILE NAME of the output being written; `@rpath/` is the modern convention, and the pair is exactly what ld64 records when no -install_name is given (the output path). WHY IT IS NOT A CONSTANT ANY MORE, and the reason is MEASURED, not stylistic: this key used to read `@rpath/libdss.dylib`, so EVERY DSS-built dylib embedded one identity -- two distinct DSS-built dylibs both named on --resolve-library produced rc 0, ZERO diagnostics, and an executable recording ONE LC_LOAD_DYLIB `@rpath/libdss.dylib`, with the second library's symbols simply absent at load, where the ELF control on the identical shape recorded TWO correct DT_NEEDED entries. The FFI recorder was not at fault: it correctly PREFERS a binary's own embedded identity over its basename (that preference is what makes a cross-compilation stand-in library work), and the two binaries were genuinely indistinguishable because this document said they were the same library. THE OLD COMMENT'S CLAIM THAT 'the walker NEVER derives it from the output file name' WAS THE DEFECT STATED AS A DISCIPLINE -- the c150 DT_SONAME rule it cited is about not INVENTING an identity silently, which this declaration does not do: the document states the shape, the walker fills exactly the declared placeholder, and an emission that cannot say which artifact it is producing is REFUSED loud (K_WalkerInputContractViolation) rather than given a fabricated one. There is deliberately NO fallback to the old constant, because a fallback here reproduces the exact collapse. A dylib that really wants a fixed identity may still declare a literal (ld64's own -install_name), and an unknown ${...} spelling is refused rather than shipped as literal text in a binary.

$staticInitializersComment:
D-C-GNU-CONSTRUCTOR-ATTRIBUTE-IS-WARNED-AND-IGNORED-NOT-RUN: THIS FORMAT DECLARES NO STATIC-INITIALIZER RUNNER, AND THE ABSENCE IS THE ANSWER -- recorded so nobody 'completes' the key by adding one.
A dylib is an IMAGE but not an EXEC flavor: `isExecFlavor()` is false, so DSS injects no entry trampoline and there is no synthesized entry to call anything. `imageLoader` would be the truthful arm -- dyld really does run a `__mod_init_func` section in a dylib -- but it requires a WRITER that emits one typed S_MOD_INIT_FUNC_POINTERS, and no DSS writer emits any static-initializer section today. Declaring either arm would therefore be false. With nothing declared, the linker REFUSES a program that schedules an initializer for this format, naming the format and the remedy -- which beats an initializer that silently never runs.

sections.$comment: Executable code. virtualAddress = 4096 = image.segmentPageSize, the base-0 dylib convention (page zero holds the header + load commands; __text opens the second page). type = 0x80000400 = S_ATTR_PURE_INSTRUCTIONS|S_ATTR_SOME_INSTRUCTIONS (the section_64.flags DSS's macho writer reads from `type`).
sections.name: __text

sections.$comment: Read-only initialized data. __TEXT,__const. virtualAddress = 0 -- computed. A reloc-bearing const global routes to relro (also __DATA,__const via the pair key).
sections.name: __const

sections.$comment: Zero-initialized data. __DATA,__bss. type = 1 = S_ZEROFILL (no file bytes). virtualAddress = 0 -- computed.
sections.name: __bss

relocations.$comment: X86_64_RELOC_BRANCH -- the extern-call reloc on a __stubs entry (a plain rel32 branch). kind = 1 matches x86_64.target.json's `rel32` row (nativeId is the packed (type<<28)|(length<<25)|(pcrel<<24)). ⚠⚠ VALUE CORRECTED 2026-08-20 (D-CONFIG-MACHO-X86_64-EXEC-DYLIB-RELOC-NATIVEID-CONTRADICTS-ITS-OWN-ROW): this row declared nativeId 369098752 = 0x16000000, which under the packing THIS COMMENT ITSELF states -- (type<<28)|(length<<25)|(pcrel<<24) -- decodes to r_type=1 (X86_64_RELOC_SIGNED), r_length=3 (8 bytes), r_pcrel=0. Every one of those three fields contradicts the row's own name and stated intent: BRANCH is r_type=2, 4 bytes, PC-relative. The `-darwin` and `-staticlib` siblings have always carried the correct 620756992 = 0x25000000 = (2<<28)|(2<<25)|(1<<24), and the arm64 family agrees on that same packed value for its own BRANCH26. ⓘ THE DEFECT WAS LATENT, NOT LIVE, AND IT IS WORTH SAYING WHICH: relocation_info records are emitted only by the MH_OBJECT writer, which reads the `-darwin`/`-staticlib` documents, so nothing consumed this number. It is corrected rather than left alone because the exec format serves a real `cli` profile with a real run leg, and a wrong declared value that no consumer reads today is precisely the shape that becomes a silent miscompile the day one does. ★ `isCall` (D-LK-MACHO-ISDATA-NO-CALL-SIGNAL, 2026-08-20): this wire relocation can ONLY target executable code, so an object reader that meets an undefined extern through it has PROVEN the extern is a function rather than a data object -- the only classification signal a symbol-name-only reference offers. It is declared HERE, on the format row, and not derived from the target's formula, because a formula describes ARITHMETIC and not ROLE: `S + A - P` is the identical arithmetic for a call and for a PC-relative data reference, so the x86_64 target's `linear` is honest and simply carries no role, while aarch64's `aarch64_call26` looked like a role only because that CPU's branch has its own instruction encoding. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-20: every macho64-x86_64 archive member calling any library function was unreadable for exactly this reason while the arm64 sibling read the same source cleanly. The target document cannot carry it -- it is PER-CPU and shared with ELF, where the same `rel32` genuinely serves data references too.
relocations.name: X86_64_RELOC_BRANCH

relocations.$comment: X86_64_RELOC_UNSIGNED (length 3 = 8 bytes) -- an abs64 data pointer; the walker emits a dyld rebase for it under the base slide. kind = 2.
relocations.name: X86_64_RELOC_UNSIGNED_8

relocations.$comment: X86_64_RELOC_UNSIGNED (length 2 = 4 bytes) -- an abs32 data slot. kind = 3. ⚠ VALUE CORRECTED 2026-08-20 (D-CONFIG-MACHO-X86_64-EXEC-DYLIB-RELOC-NATIVEID-CONTRADICTS-ITS-OWN-ROW): declared 33554432 = 0x02000000, which is r_length=1 = TWO bytes, for a row named _4 and (in the dylib sibling) commented "length 2 = 4 bytes". The correct packing is (0<<28)|(2<<25)|(0<<24) = 0x04000000 = 67108864, which is what the `-darwin`/`-staticlib` siblings carry. Same latency as the BRANCH row above: the MH_OBJECT writer is the only consumer of these numbers and it reads a different document.
relocations.name: X86_64_RELOC_UNSIGNED_4
